correctness.rationale: The complete-prism geodesics of length two have two possible internal vertices. Every omitted vertex forces its matching counterpart to be selected. With a doubled column, distinct selected endpoint pairs cover every omission; without one, the cross-pair counting obstruction and explicit distinct-pair construction give an exact iff criterion. Three-state counting and single-deletion tests determine both polynomials. Minimum solutions are matching transversals and the token-jumping graph is a middle-rank cube, whose isometric property follows from a boundary-respecting bit-flip ordering. The independent BFS and matching algorithm exhaustively checked all 21,840 subsets for n=2,...,7; finite checks supplement rather than prove the general statement.

value.rationale: The earlier Cartesian-product result gives a single optimum cardinality; the all-budget feasible-set polynomial counts every terminal placement, while the minimal polynomial determines deletion-irreducible sets and the new strong upper geodetic value. The sharp jump from six isolated minimum solutions at n=4 to a connected isometric rank-selected hypercube of diameter n for all n>=5 quantifies the navigation between optimum terminal placements. These naturally motivated structural invariants are not a mere scalar restatement or a known-table recomputation.
